evals.prompt: Hey, can you write up the release notes for Cereal v2.3.0? The repo is at /tmp/cereal-fake-repo. Use the commits since the last tag (v2.2.0..v2.3.0).
evals.expected_output: All five outputs generated: a Discord announcement, Instagram caption, X thread (3-7 tweets), a formal markdown changelog, and a short blog post. The file is saved as cereal-v2.3.0-release-notes-<date>.md. Features and fixes are highlighted. Internal/chore commits appear only in the formal changelog.
expectations: A Discord announcement section is present with bold headers and bullet points
An Instagram caption is present, uses flowing prose (not bullet points), and ends with hashtags
An X thread is present with at least 3 separate tweets, each under 280 characters
A formal changelog section is present using Keep a Changelog format with ### Added / ### Fixed headers
A blog post section is present, written in prose (not bullet lists), 200-400 words, with subheadings like 'What's new' or 'Fixes and improvements'
The output is saved to a .md file
Chore/CI commits are excluded from Discord, Instagram, and blog content
Feature commits are prominently highlighted in Discord, X, and blog sections

evals.prompt: Write release notes for the Cereal app version 1.0.0 — it's a big milestone release! Repo path: /tmp/cereal-v1-repo. Show me the range v0.9.5..v1.0.0.
evals.expected_output: Release notes treating this as a milestone release. Discord post acknowledges the v1.0 milestone with appropriate excitement. Instagram and X treat it as a major launch moment. Formal changelog is complete and structured.
expectations: Discord section acknowledges v1.0 as a milestone (e.g., uses words like '1.0', 'milestone', or similar celebratory language)
Instagram caption has a hook that conveys a major launch
X thread has a hook tweet that calls out the v1.0 milestone
Formal changelog uses ## [1.0.0] header
Blog post treats v1.0 as a milestone with a slightly longer intro or closing reflection
All five sections are present in the output file

evals.prompt: Quick patch release — Cereal v2.4.1 has just a few bug fixes. Repo is at /tmp/cereal-patch-repo, range v2.4.0..v2.4.1. Keep things appropriately low-key.
evals.expected_output: Release notes sized appropriately for a small patch. Discord post is brief and doesn't oversell. Instagram and X are short. Formal changelog still complete. No invented features.
expectations: Discord section is concise — not inflated with fake excitement for a patch release
X thread is short (3-4 tweets max for a patch)
Instagram caption reflects patch scope (not written like a major launch)
Formal changelog is present with ## [2.4.1] header
Blog post is short (under ~200 words is appropriate for a patch) and does not oversell
No content is fabricated — if commits are few, output is appropriately brief
